title: S3 and a local SQLite file for snapshots and results

questions.heading: Every Write Is Conditional: S3 Refuses to Replace an Object
questions.stem: A worker's put_result for run-0042 is sent again after a network error, but the first write had in fact reached S3. With the lesson's store, what happens to the second write?

options.text: It replaces the first object with the same bytes, so the run's result is unchanged
options.says: Every write is conditional: with If-None-Match: *, S3 refuses to write over an existing object.

options.text: S3 refuses it with 412, and put_result raises: a result is already there
options.says: Right: a result that already exists is an error; the output shows 'second result for run-0007 refused'.

options.text: S3 refuses it with 412, and put_result counts it a success, as put_snapshot does
options.says: Only an existing snapshot is fine (same key, same content); 'a result that already exists is an error'.

options.text: S3 keeps it as a second version, and put_result returns the newer version's key
options.says: A conditional write succeeds only if no object exists at the key; otherwise it fails with 412.

questions.heading: Every Read Re-Hashes, and Versioning Keeps What an Overwrite Replaced
questions.stem: In the lesson's versioned bucket, someone writes new bytes over a snapshot's key with a plain put_object, no condition. What happens next?

options.text: A read is refused as corrupted, and the earlier version is still kept and re-hashes to its key
options.says: Right: get_snapshot re-hashes and refuses; the output shows 2 versions, the earlier one re-hashing to its key.

options.text: A read of it is refused as corrupted, and the earlier version is gone, as the key holds new bytes
options.says: Versioning keeps every version: the output shows 'versions kept: 2'.

options.text: A read of it returns the new bytes, as S3 checked their checksum when they were written
options.says: get_snapshot hashes the bytes and compares with the key; the output shows the read refused.

options.text: The write is refused with 412, as every object in a versioned bucket can be written only once
options.says: The unconditional overwrite succeeded; only writes sent with If-None-Match: * are refused.

questions.heading: The Index Can Be Rebuilt From S3, Except for Runs Still Waiting
questions.stem: The API's SQLite index file is lost. At that moment three runs had finished and two were still waiting. What does rebuilding it from S3 give back?

options.text: The five runs, as a run's index row is copied to S3 when the run is submitted
options.says: Nothing in S3 says a waiting run exists; the rebuild of the lesson gave 2 rows of 3.

options.text: The three run ids, while their statuses and NPVs stay behind in the lost index
options.says: Every result object carries its run id, digest, status and NPV; the rebuilt rows print 'optimal' and the NPV.

options.text: The three finished runs; the two waiting ones come back by asking Step Functions
options.says: Right: only runs with a result object are rebuilt; after a rebuild, ask Step Functions for the executions still running.

options.text: The three finished runs; the two waiting ones are lost along with the index file
options.says: The lesson: ask Step Functions for the executions still running to recover the waiting runs.
